newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Gilt, short stg vols shrug off rate nerves.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Gilt, short stg vols shrug off rate nerves.

text.p: Gilt and short sterling options volatility remained flat on Thursday, shrugging off concerns over a possible British rate hike following a UK monetary meeting.
Traders said activity was slim, particularly in the gilts sector, and implied volatilities were broadly unchanged from levels earlier in the week.
"The vol hasn't really moved. At the moment it seems to be 50-50 between hiking 25 (basis points) to no hike," said Luke White, senior options broker at Fimat Banque in London.
The Bank of England's new monetary policy committee begins its first meeting on Thursday on whether to raise rates from 6.25 percent amid mixed inflationary signals.

Interest rate futures are factoring in a rise of about a quarter-point at some point soon. But economists said a hike, and the possible result of a rise in sterling, would hurt manufacturing output growth which has been sluggish.
A Reuters poll of 21 economists showed a narrow majority anticipated a rate rise from present 6.25 percent.

In options, September short sterling at-the-money vols were steady at around 8.50 percent, March at 12 percent and December at 10 percent. September gilt vols were at 7.30 percent compared with 7.40 on Wednesday.
Thursday's short sterling trades featured June 93.50 puts at 15 percent vol compared with around 12.25 on Wednesday.
In March, a 92.75-93.25 call spread traded 300 times, traders said.
"People are interested in call ladders," White said. "They want to get short on the upside calls and just lean on it as a vol trade," said White.
Activity was also thinned by apprehension ahead of U.S. non-farm payrolls data on Friday that is expected to set the stage for a rate rise in July.

"Most people are not going to put on any positions," White said, because even if positions they put on are correct in terms of the view on interest rates, there is a chance the payrolls data will go against them.
